notes: No live Codex event delivery has been observed. codex.cli is fixture-level: installation, placeholder rendering, and normalization are fixture-covered. codex.desktop stays unverified because delivery for an ordinary local desktop chat is unproven.

Installed entries are inline [[hooks.<Event>]] tables in ~/.codex/config.toml. Codex skips untrusted non-managed hooks, so open /hooks in Codex once, review the seven AwakeLite entries, and trust them. Editing the block later changes each handler hash and requires a new review.
Every handler is a background command hook: it never delays a turn, blocks a tool, answers an approval prompt, continues a turn, or adds model context.
Restart Codex after install so the configuration reloads. Hooks are enabled by default; if hooks were disabled in Codex settings, AwakeLite does not re-enable them.

Both steps share one asset, so one family install writes two blocks (one per target) and Codex runs each event once per target. Every event carries its own --target, and the model keeps one work record per turn, so state converges; the cost is two short-lived helper runs per event.

Local and cloud orchestration differ: the vendor contract excludes local command hooks from cloud orchestration, so cloud-orchestrated work is not observed and no work is invented. An ordinary local desktop chat is still unverified.
